transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-16 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), James Wong (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (CTO - OptiHealth), Lena Ortiz (ML Eng), Tom Reeves (SRE)

Summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results (latency p50/p95, throughput tokens/sec) comparing Redwood Dedicated config vs the customer's current baseline provider (BaselineCloud). Discussion covered batching, KV cache effects, quantization tradeoffs, and parity tests to isolate infra differences. Agreed next steps to run identical-config parity tests and share full logs/spreadsheet.

[00:00] Maya: ok great everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick rund- run through the benchmark numbers we sent earlier and then go into tuning recommendations. James will jump into the charts after I set context.
[00:18] Priya: thanks, our main goal today is to see if the latency improvements are real at our 2k rps and typical sequence lengths, and what efforts are needed to get parity with current infra.
[00:28] James: yep makes sense, we'll focus on p50/p95 and tokens per second, and then go through config diffs. I have the run for redwood-dedicated on an A100 pool vs their baseline on BaselineCloud that used mixed VMs.
[00:42] Lena: quick note, our baseline numbers were from yesterday's run with the 13B model, 1k max tokens, batch window 50ms, not the trimmed smaller loads.
[00:56] James: got it. Ok slide 1, p50 numbers: Redwood Dedicated median around 75ms for our 13B quantized profile, BaselineCloud p50 was ~140ms. p95 for Redwood about 220ms, BaselineCloud p95 about 480ms. These are median numbers across the 10k trace.
[01:20] Tom: that seems like a big delta, are we sure sequences and tokenization match? sometimes tokenization differences inflate latency.
[01:30] James: good call, we did normalize tokenization, same tokenizer and model weights. where there's some noise is the GPU type and the batching logic — BaselineCloud was on older T4-like instances in some runs, occasionally mixed, which increases tail latency.
[01:50] Priya: our prod environment will likely be H100s though; would that narrow the gap?
[01:58] James: H100s will help both providers, but Redwood's kernel selection and KV caching gives us an edge on small-request latency. With H100 the p50 drops to ~60ms and p95 to ~180ms in our tests.
[02:15] Maya: also worth noting we enabled prefix KV cache for the steady-state prompt set — that shaved ~20-30% off token generation time for repeated prefixes, which your traffic has a lot of.
[02:28] Lena: wait you said KV cache — sorry auto transcription said KV cash on the doc, lol — yes we have many repeated system prompts. can we see numbers with cache disabled?
[02:37] James: yes the spreadsheet has both. with cache disabled Redwood p50 moves to ~95ms and p95 to ~280ms; BaselineCloud also sees uplift but still higher tails.
[02:50] Tom: how about throughput? our target is 2k rps with average 200 token responses. numbers per GPU or cluster?
[02:59] James: our throughput numbers reported as tokens/sec per GPU: Redwood peak sustained ~920 tokens/sec per A100; BaselineCloud around 350 tokens/sec per equivalent GPU in their mixed runs. At your expected load that maps to fewer GPUs for Redwood, hence cost savings.
[03:20] Priya: curious about quantization — you're running 4-bit or 8-bit? we've been hesitant on agressive quant for quality.
[03:28] James: we're using 4-bit PTQ (int4-like) for this profile; quality checks on the evaluation prompts showed negligible regressions vs float16 for your use-case. We also have a 8-bit/float16 fallback profile if you want conservative ops.
[03:42] Lena: can you share the eval prompts and delta metrics? we need to show product owners.
[03:47] Maya: yes, that's in the shared drive — the spreadsheet includes PPL deltas, Rouge-like scores and a handful of human eval notes. I'll attach links after the call.
[03:57] Priya: on cost: does Redwood include preemptible options? right now BaselineCloud used preemptible and that influenced their perf variability.
[04:07] James: Redwood Dedicated in this pilot used reserved A100s for stable perf; we can show a mixed reserved+burst approach but for apples-to-apples we kept reserved. Preemptibles will generally increase tail latency.
[04:20] Tom: anything in the config that could explain BaselineCloud's 480ms p95 — is it batching latency, or network?
[04:28] James: two things — they had a larger batching window in their agent (100ms) to amortize cost, and also their KV caching wasn't enabled. both increase p95. We saw spikes correlated with batching windows.
[04:40] Priya: ok seems sensible. what's the recommended tuning if we wanted to optimize for 95th percentile?
[04:47] James: reduce max batch window to 25-40ms for latency sensitive routes, enable KV prefix caching where applicable, use smaller max tokens for interactive endpoints, and enable continuous batching with adaptive heuristics. Also consider quantization profile that matches your quality targets.
[05:05] Maya: and from ops side we'll provide a runbook with exact config keys: batch_window_ms, max_batch_tokens, cache_ttl, model_variant, quant_profile.
[05:14] Lena: super. about parity tests — are you willing to help run identical configs on BaselineCloud so we can isolate infra vs runtime differences?
[05:22] Maya: yes we'll help. James will run a parity job with identical model binary, tokenizer, sequence-length distribution, and batch config and share raw logs so you can diff.
[05:32] James: one caveat — we may not be able to run your exact BaselineCloud binaries but we'll match the model weights and config as closely as possible; small runtime differences may persist.
[05:44] Priya: that's fine as long as we get a reasonable comparison. Tom can provide BaselineCloud run artifacts if you need them.
[05:50] Tom: yes we can share their perf logs and instance types.
[05:54] James: perfect. quick note on seq length: your median sequence in traces is 180 tokens, top 95th is 420 tokens, so the cost and latency curves change a lot above 256 tokens. we included segmented metrics in the spreadsheet.
[06:12] Lena: the tail gets worse on Baseline for >256, correct?
[06:16] James: yes, we saw p95 jump more dramatically on BaselineCloud above 256 because their kernels don't fuse as effectively and their KV cache is off.
[06:26] Priya: any security or compliance blockers for dedicated/private?
[06:29] Maya: for Private we support VPC, KMS integration, audit logs and SOC2 controls. For this POC Dedicated, we have audit logs and network isolation options; we'll share the security pack docs in the next step.
[06:41] Priya: great. one more: can we run a small on-prem parity with our H100 cluster?
[06:48] James: yes we can do a private deployment test — need access and a runbook, but we can target that after parity on BaselineCloud.
[06:56] Maya: ok let's recap quickly the action items and next steps. James will run parity runs on BaselineCloud and share logs by the 23rd; I'll send the full spreadsheet and runbook by the 18th; OptiHealth to provide traces and confirm GPU type by the 20th; schedule follow-up for the 24th to review.
[07:15] Priya: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side for timeline?
[07:19] James: no blockers, just need BaselineCloud access and your traces.
[07:23] Tom: I'll put the BaselineCloud perf bundle in the shared folder today.
[07:27] Lena: and I'll upload the prompt set and traces by Sunday.
[07:31] Maya: perfect. we'll also include cost estimates comparing per-token + reserved capacity math and show how batch tuning changes unit cost.
[07:40] Priya: thanks, one last question — when you mention tokens/sec per GPU, does that include decoding overhead for streaming responses?
[07:47] James: good question — tokens/sec is measured end-to-end generation; streaming overhead is small but included. throughput for small chunk sizes will be slightly lower due to RPC overhead, we have numbers for chunked vs batch full.
[08:02] Priya: ok that's enough for now. thanks everyone.

Recap (end of meeting):
- Redwood shows materially lower p50/p95 vs BaselineCloud in current tests; primary drivers are kernel/runtime optimizations, KV cache, and batching config.
- Action items + owners as listed.
- Next call to review parity results and discuss private deployment pilot (proposed 2025-07-24).
